subject: Social Habits
title: Giving and being grateful
subtopics: Saying thank you for gifts and help
objectives: Children will say thank you and say what they are thankful for.
Children will give or share with others.
content: Saying thank you for gifts and help, giving to others, and sharing food and toys.
teachingActivities: Link gratitude to real things children notice (food, rain, family, teachers); let children give freely and never force giving; model generosity and thanks; respect families who have less and avoid asking for gifts or money; keep any food activity allergy-safe.
learnerActivities: Say what they are thankful for and give or share with a friend.
resources: A thank-you tree made of paper
assessment: Observe whether each child says what they are thankful for and gives or shares with a friend.
expectedOutcomes: Says what they are thankful for.
Gives or shares an item with a friend.

lessons.title: Being thankful
lessons.subject: Social Habits
lessons.subtopic: Saying thank you for gifts and help
objectives: Children will say what they are thankful for.
successCriteria: Says one thing they are thankful for
Says thank you with a smile
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can say thank you, share and help others.
resources: Pictures of food, family, rain and friends
lessons.starter: Show a paper tree with no leaves and say "Our tree is bare. We will add leaves for things we are thankful for."
teacherActivities: Show pictures of food, family, rain and friends and say "I am thankful for this."
Ask "What are you thankful for?" and listen.
Help each child draw or place a leaf on the tree.
Say "We say thank you for good things."
learnerActivities: Child names or points to something.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show pictures of food, family, rain and friends and say "I am thankful for this." Children: Children look and say thankful.
Step 2. Teacher: Ask "What are you thankful for?" and listen. Children: Child names or points to something.
Step 3. Teacher: Help each child draw or place a leaf on the tree. Children: Child places a leaf.
Step 4. Teacher: Say "We say thank you for good things." Children: Children repeat the sentence.

practical.title: Thank-you tree
steps: Choose something you are thankful for.
Put the leaf on the tree.
practical.safety: Use non-toxic crayons and keep paper away from mouths. Accept every answer and never compare what children have.

differentiation.support: Offer two pictures and help the child choose.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to say why they are thankful.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

expectedOutcomes: Says what they are thankful for
Says thank you with a smile
lessons.conclusion: Look at the full tree and say "Thank you."
lessons.homeConnection: Say one thing you are thankful for with your child each evening.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "say what they are thankful for" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

learnerFacing.songOrRhyme: Thank you for the sun, thank you for the rain.

lessons.title: Giving to others
lessons.subject: Social Habits
objectives: Children will give something to a friend or helper.
successCriteria: Gives a drawing or toy to a friend
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can say thank you, share and help others.
lessons.starter: Show a drawing and say "I made this for you. This is a gift."
teacherActivities: Show how to draw something for a friend.
Let each child draw or pick something to give.
Help children give their gift and say this is for you.
learnerActivities: Child gives and says this is for you.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show how to draw something for a friend. Children: Children watch.
Step 2. Teacher: Let each child draw or pick something to give. Children: Child draws or chooses.
Step 3. Teacher: Help children give their gift and say this is for you. Children: Child gives and says this is for you.
Step 4. Teacher: Say "Giving makes us happy." Children: Children smile.

practical.title: A gift for a friend
steps: Give it and say this is for you.
practical.safety: Use non-toxic crayons and make sure every child gets a gift so none is left out. Never ask for money or valuable gifts.

differentiation.extension: Ask the child to give a gift to a helper.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

expectedOutcomes: Gives a gift to a friend
lessons.homeConnection: Let your child give a drawing to someone.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "give something to a friend or helper" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Sharing food and toys
lessons.subject: Social Habits
objectives: Children will share toys and, with care, food in a small group.
successCriteria: Passes pretend food to a friend
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can say thank you, share and help others.
lessons.starter: Spread a picnic blanket and say "We are having a picnic. We share with friends."
teacherActivities: Show how to pass a plate and say please and thank you.
Give each child toy food to share.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show how to pass a plate and say please and thank you. Children: Children watch.
Step 2. Teacher: Give each child toy food to share. Children: Child passes toy food.
Step 3. Teacher: Share toys at the picnic. Children: Child shares a toy.
Step 4. Teacher: Say "Sharing is kind." Children: Children repeat the sentence.

practical.title: Picnic sharing
practical.safety: Use toy food only for this activity. If real snacks are shared, check allergies and seat children while they eat.

differentiation.extension: Ask the child to serve every friend.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: What do we do with food?

lessons.conclusion: Tidy the picnic and say "Thank you."
lessons.homeConnection: Share a snack with a sibling and say thank you.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "share toys and, with care, food in a small group" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Thank you circle
lessons.subject: Social Habits
lessons.subtopic: Saying thank you for gifts and help
objectives: Children will thank a friend for something kind in a circle.
successCriteria: Says thank you to a friend
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can say thank you, share and help others.
lessons.starter: Roll the ball to a child and say "Thank you for being kind today."
teacherActivities: Show how to pass the ball and thank the friend for something.
Pass the ball around the circle.
Help children say what the friend did.
learnerActivities: Child says thank you to the next friend.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show how to pass the ball and thank the friend for something. Children: Children watch.
Step 2. Teacher: Pass the ball around the circle. Children: Child says thank you to the next friend.
Step 3. Teacher: Help children say what the friend did. Children: Child says shared or helped.
Step 4. Teacher: Say "Thank you, everyone." Children: Children clap and cheer.

practical.title: Thank you ball
practical.safety: Use a soft ball and sit children away from furniture. Make sure every child receives thanks.

differentiation.support: Pass the ball together and say thank you.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to thank a friend for something specific.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

expectedOutcomes: Says thank you to a friend
lessons.homeConnection: Thank each family member for something small.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "thank a friend for something kind in a circle" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Week 7 gratitude check
lessons.subject: Social Habits
objectives: Teachers will observe how each child shows gratitude and generosity.
successCriteria: Says what they are thankful for
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can say thank you, share and help others.
lessons.starter: Sing the thank you song and show three stations.
teacherActivities: Set up three stations: thankful tree, giving and sharing.
At each station watch how the child behaves.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Set up three stations: thankful tree, giving and sharing. Children: Children rotate every four minutes.
Step 2. Teacher: At each station watch how the child behaves. Children: Child responds with a prompt.
Step 3. Teacher: Record each child’s level. Children: Children tidy at the signal.

practical.title: Gratitude stations
practical.safety: Supervise each station and keep floors clear. Use toy food only and non-toxic materials.

differentiation.support: Provide an adult partner and use one station.
differentiation.extension: Ask a confident child to thank a helper.

assessment.method: Observe and record Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding for: says what they are thankful for; says thank you; gives a gift; shares toys.

questions.question: What do we do with toys?

expectedOutcomes: Has an observation record for Week 7
Shows gratitude and generosity with support
lessons.conclusion: Wave goodbye and say well done.
lessons.homeConnection: Keep saying thank you and sharing at home.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "Teachers will observe how each child shows gratitude and generosity" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?
